note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old man with several months of low mood, low energy and appetite, ~1 stone weight loss over ~6 months, and episodic palpitations/shortness of breath most notable in lifts; plan to obtain baseline blood tests.

History:
- Presenting complaint: several months of low mood, decreased energy and appetite; noted weight loss and episodic palpitations/shortness of breath.
- Onset/duration/progression:
  - Low mood/low energy/appetite began after changing to a new law firm ~3–3.5 months ago (patient states symptoms started then).
  - Weight loss began earlier and has progressed over approximately 6 months; patient estimates ~1 stone total loss.
  - Episodic palpitations and difficulty breathing occur notably when in lifts and on other occasions; patient denies chest pain.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Intermittent nausea (not associated with vomiting).
  - Occasional headaches.
  - Reports reduced sexual/nightly activity per spouse’s comment.
  - Can perform work duties but has some difficulty at times.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No chest pain reported.
  - Bowel function described as normal: no diarrheal episodes, no blood or mucus, and no vomiting.
- Past medical history and medications:
  - History of hypothyroidism (patient describes "too little activity of my thyroid").
  - Previously took thyroxine but stopped taking it since changing doctor; current thyroxine use: not taking — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - No recent blood tests; "haven't taken one in a long time."
- Social history and preventive care:
  - Occupation: lawyer.
  - Married (spouse has noted change in "nightly activities").
  - Currently not walking/exercising much.
  - No details documented on smoking, alcohol, drug use, or mental health risk screening.

Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination findings: none documented.

Impression:
- Low mood/depressive symptoms with decreased appetite, low energy and unintentional weight loss (~1 stone over ~6 months).
- Episodic palpitations and subjective shortness of breath, particularly in lifts.
- History of hypothyroidism off thyroxine treatment; biochemical causes (including thyroid dysfunction, anemia, vitamin deficiency) were considered by clinician.

Plan:
- Obtain a general set of blood tests to investigate causes of symptoms (clinician stated tests to assess anemia, kidney function, liver function, and vitamin levels).
- Advise patient to contact support via the app (phone number provided in app) to arrange blood tests; clinician will complete form to facilitate this.
- Patient will receive a text message instructing how to book follow-up once results are available.
- If blood tests are normal, a physical examination will be arranged as the next step.
- Safety/advice:
  - If chest pain or severe palpitations occur, go to Emergency Department (A&E) urgently.
  - If bowel habits change or patient develops vomiting, contact the service promptly.
- Follow-up: arranged after blood test results; patient instructed to re-contact sooner if worsening.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies: not documented.
  - Complete current medication list and doses (thyroxine dose/route/frequency not documented; other medications not documented).
  - Vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, temperature).
  - Mental health risk assessment (suicidal ideation, self-harm screening) and formal mood/suicide screen.
  - Specific blood tests ordered (exact panels/tests and whether thyroid function tests included were not explicitly documented).
  - Smoking, alcohol, and substance use history.
  - Exact weight measurements and dates.
  - Date when thyroxine was stopped and last TSH/thyroid function test results.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Patient reports history of hypothyroidism and has stopped thyroxine, yet current symptoms (palpitations, tachycardia-like sensations) are classically more typical of hyperthyroid states — clinician noted the picture is unclear (conflict noted).
  - Timeline: patient states appetite loss started ~3–3.5 months ago but weight loss began earlier (~6 months); both statements documented.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall understandable but contains sections with overlapping speech and a few inaudible or truncated phrases; moderate clarity with occasional missing words.
